rules.instruction: When the description says the process begins when an actor performs an action of its own, such as identifying a need, rather than when an external message or condition arrives: Model a plain start event for the stated beginning of the process, with a label that names only the trigger state and not the actor's action. Model the actor's action as a task placed after the start event and connected to it by a sequence flow, and keep that task before the next described step. rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity may also be performed as an optional extra step, on top of the main path, so it is not performed in every case (signalled by wording such as 'may also'): Place an exclusive gateway on the path at the point where the optional activity could occur. Give the optional activity its own outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, and give a bypass flow that skips it. Merge the optional branch and the bypass with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Keep the required activities on the main path unconditional and do not drop the optional activity.

Do not merge the clauses into one task with a joined label, even when one clause reads as a summary of the other.

Merge the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Do not drop any named alternative and do not leave the choice as one unconditional flow.
